MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Musa has one Ksh 100 note, one Ksh 50 note and two Ksh 20 coins. How much money does he have? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 150
   B. Ksh 210
   C. Ksh 170
   D. Ksh 190

2. What is 92 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 33
   B. 22
   C. 23
   D. 24

3. Work out 1,204 + 1,315. (1 mark)
   A. 2,529
   B. 3,519
   C. 2,519
   D. 2,419

4. In the fraction 7/8, what does the numerator 7 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. The number of wholes
   B. The size of each part in centimetres
   C. How many equal parts the whole has
   D. How many of the equal parts are taken

5. What does 4m mean? (1 mark)
   A. 4 + m
   B. 4 − m
   C. 4 × m
   D. 4 ÷ m

6. What is 48 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 96
   B. 9,600
   C. 960
   D. 68

7. Two lines that meet at a point form (1 mark)
   A. a circle
   B. a triangle
   C. a square
   D. an angle

8. Which sum checks that 5,432 − 2,718 = 2,714? (1 mark)
   A. 2,714 + 2,718
   B. 5,432 + 2,718
   C. 5,432 + 2,714
   D. 2,714 − 2,718

9. Why do people prepare a shopping list? (1 mark)
   A. To buy as many things as possible
   B. To make shops close early
   C. To remember everything and not spend more than they have
   D. To avoid using money

10. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many more are there of matatu than of boda boda? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 4
   C. 7
   D. 3

11. What number is the Roman numeral IV? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 5
   C. 7
   D. 6

12. Write 0.05 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5/10
   B. 5/1000
   C. 50/100
   D. 5/100

13. What is 10 kg − 3 1/2 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 6 1/2 kg
   B. 7 kg
   C. 6 3/4 kg
   D. 6 1/4 kg

14. What is 3 1/2 L + 1 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/2 L
   B. 4 3/4 L
   C. 5 1/4 L
   D. 5 L

15. Work out 36 × 24. (1 mark)
   A. 854
   B. 216
   C. 874
   D. 864

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. 45 eggs are packed in trays that hold 6 eggs each. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? Explain. (3 marks)

17. How many right angles does a rectangle have? Explain. (2 marks)

18. Work out 36 × 24 by first multiplying by the ones and then by the tens. (3 marks)

19. Work out 6,003 − 2,475 and check your answer by adding. (4 marks)

20. Express 23/6 as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Ksh 190
   100 + 50 + 20 + 20 = 190.

2. C — 23
   4 × 23 = 92, so 92 ÷ 4 = 23.

3. C — 2,519
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 1,204 + 1,315 = 2,519.

4. D — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 7/8 it says that 7 parts are taken.

5. C — 4 × m
   A number written next to a letter means multiply. 4m is 4 times m.

6. C — 960
   48 × 2 = 96, then × 10 gives 960.

7. D — an angle
   When two lines meet at a point they make an angle.

8. A — 2,714 + 2,718
   Addition undoes subtraction. 2,714 + 2,718 = 5,432, the starting number.

9. C — To remember everything and not spend more than they have
   A list helps us remember what we need and plan our spending.

10. D — 3
   5 − 2 = 3.

11. A — 4
   IV stands for 4.

12. D — 5/100
   The last digit of 0.05 is in the hundredths place, so the denominator is 100. 0.05 = 5/100.

13. A — 6 1/2 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 10 kg − 3 1/2 kg = 6 1/2 kg.

14. B — 4 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 1/2 L + 1 1/4 L = 4 3/4 L.

15. D — 864
   36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720. 144 + 720 = 864.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 trays
   Working / marking points: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3 (1 mark). Seven trays are full (1 mark). The 3 left-over eggs need another tray, so 8 trays (1 mark).

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4. A rectangle has four corners and each corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 and 1 mark for the reason.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: 864
   Working / marking points: 36 × 4 = 144 (1 mark); 36 × 20 = 720 (1 mark); 144 + 720 = 864 (1 mark).

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct regrouping across the zeros, 1 mark for the answer, 1 mark for the check.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 5/6
   Working / marking points: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5 (2 marks). Write 3 5/6 with the same denominator (1 mark).
